definition: the rule that a relationship needs a row I come out behind on, and what it costs her

settled:
Relationships require sacrifice to exist. I have taken that as a rule I run rather than as something I noticed.

What the word means for me is a position in the ledger: a negative value of mine on a positive-sum row. One row, two entries, the total positive, mine the negative one. A relationship with no such row does not exist.

That is stronger than the blank check being one way to run a marriage. It says some rows I come out behind on are the condition of there being a relationship at all.

Her entry is not free either. Put to me that a night costing us both would be a row my model has no slot for, I said it costs her, but also benefits her, leaving her net positive, but she still notices the cost.

So the row stays positive-sum and mine stays the negative entry. What is added is that hers carries a cost inside a positive total, and that cost is one she notices.

title: What Sacrifice Means In The Ledger
